<h1>Learn age-period-cohort analysis with matisseR</h1>

## What you will learn

<ul class="outcomes">
<li>Organize cases and person-years into Lexis diagrams and <code>rates</code> objects.</li>
<li>Fit the New APC model and read its estimable functions and net drift.</li>
<li>Test whether two or more groups share the same age, period and cohort patterns (CAPRICORN).</li>
<li>Compare social generations with their proxy parents and pool results across populations.</li>
<li>Estimate the fitted cohort share of a cause among all deaths or cases.</li>
<li>Structure an analysis so that others can rerun and check it.</li>
</ul>

<ul class="skills" aria-label="Skills you will gain">
<li>Age-period-cohort analysis</li><li>Lexis diagrams</li><li>Rate ratios</li><li>Comparative analysis</li><li>Social generations</li><li>Disease surveillance</li><li>Reproducible R workflows</li>
</ul>

## Learn from two real projects

Modules 2 to 4 show figures from real research projects built with `matisseR`. Read them as a learner, then run the same ideas on the synthetic example data.

<a class="case" href="cases/eu-generations.html"><div class="thumb"><img src="images/cases/eu_anatomy_apc.png" alt="Anatomy of the New APC model: observed rates, fitted cohort pattern, local drifts and temporal trend"></div><div class="txt"><strong>Cancer in successive generations in Europe</strong><span>Are younger generations at higher risk of cancer than their parents' generation? 21 European populations and 17 cancers.</span><em>Open case study →</em></div></a>

## Live workshop

A live workshop will use this course as its guide. Attendees work through selected modules with the team and ask questions. The format and dates will be announced on the [Live workshop](workshop.qmd) page.

## FAQ {#faq}

<div class="syllabus">
<details class="mod"><summary><span class="mt"><strong>Do I need to know R already?</strong></span><span class="tog" aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><div class="body"><p>Basic R helps: running code, reading a table, drawing a plot with ggplot2. Module 0 gets you set up, and every code sample runs as written. You do not need any APC background.</p></div></details>
<details class="mod"><summary><span class="mt"><strong>Do I have to pay for anything?</strong></span><span class="tog" aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><div class="body"><p>No. R, RStudio and matisseR are free. The MATLAB toolbox in Module 5 needs MATLAB, but you can use MATLAB Online in your browser with a MathWorks account; check MathWorks's current access terms.</p></div></details>
<details class="mod"><summary><span class="mt"><strong>Is the real data in the case studies available?</strong></span><span class="tog" aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><div class="body"><p>The code samples use synthetic datasets that ship with the package, so you can run everything yourself. The case-study figures come from research in progress, and their data come from public sources such as the WHO Mortality Database and European cancer registries.</p></div></details>
<details class="mod"><summary><span class="mt"><strong>Is matisseR peer reviewed or published?</strong></span><span class="tog" aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><div class="body"><p>The methods are published; see the <a href="resources.html#papers">method papers</a>. The R package is version 0.1.0 and is being developed. It has an internal test suite, and its comparison with the MATLAB toolbox is in preparation.</p></div></details>
<details class="mod"><summary><span class="mt"><strong>How do I ask a question?</strong></span><span class="tog" aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><div class="body"><p>Write to <a href="mailto:matisse.apc@gmail.com">matisse.apc@gmail.com</a>. Every function also has a help page in R, for example <code>?apc_fit</code>.</p></div></details>
</div>
